verdict.rationale: Paxos documents a conventional OAuth2-secured v2 API for transfers, conversions, deposit addresses and one-call mint/redeem orchestrations, so developers move stablecoins and crypto through API calls rather than operating chains themselves. The evidence never explicitly says nodes and gas are abstracted, and it shows no client libraries or SDKs; the OpenAPI probe also returned 404. missing for 10: explicit documentation that nodes, gas and chain mechanics are handled by Paxos, official client libraries/SDKs in common languages, a published OpenAPI spec, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I never operate blockchain infrastructure — the platform abstracts nodes, gas, and chain mechanics behind a conventional REST API with client libraries in my language

citations.quote: Convert USD to Stablecoins and transfer all in one call.
Convert stablecoins to USD and withdraw to your bank in one call.
Get market data, create orders, execute held-rate quotes, and transfer assets with Paxos API v2.0.
Accept PYUSD, USDC and USDP payments via on-chain transfers.
Paxos APIs use OAuth 2 with the client credentials grant flow.
